items.name: Sabudana Kheer
steps: Rinse or wipe the dry tapioca pearls (sabudana) as appropriate and coat it with the ghee in a heavy pan.
Pour in the milk and bring it slowly to a simmer, stirring across the base of the pan.
Cook gently until the dry tapioca pearls (sabudana) is fully tender and the milk lightly thickens.
Add the rock sugar and saffron strands; simmer only until dissolved.
Crush in the cardamom, rest for five minutes, and serve warm or at room temperature.
items.guidance: Sabudana Kheer is a rich milk sweet intended as a small, freshly prepared portion. Vata: serve warm with the stated ghee. Pitta: use less sugar and favor cardamom or saffron. Kapha: take only a small portion and do not serve chilled.

items.name: Gajar Halwa (Ghee-Milk)
steps: Prepare the carrot, finely grated finely so it cooks to an even texture.
Warm half the ghee in a heavy pan and cook the main ingredient slowly until its raw aroma fades.
Add the milk and raisins, almonds, chopped; simmer, stirring often, until absorbed.
Stir in the jaggery and remaining ghee; cook until the mixture gathers softly from the pan.
Finish with crushed cardamom and serve warm in small portions.
items.guidance: Gajar Halwa (Ghee-Milk) is a slow-cooked festive sweet, best treated as a modest accompaniment rather than a main meal. Vata: serve warm and soft. Pitta: reduce sweetener and emphasize cardamom. Kapha: take the smallest portion and reduce ghee if preparing at home.

items.name: Dry Fruit Ladoo (No Sugar)
steps: Toast the almonds over low heat until aromatic, then cool slightly.
Grind or crush it to the texture specified by the style, leaving a little body rather than making a paste.
Warm the ghee with cardamom and combine it with the soft dates and walnuts, dried figs, chopped.
Mix with the toasted base until the mixture holds when pressed; let it cool enough to handle.
Shape into 14 small balls and allow them to set before serving.
items.guidance: Dry Fruit Ladoo (No Sugar) is a compact traditional sweet; one small piece is the intended serving. Vata: take it warm or at room temperature. Pitta: use the lower sweetener amount and cooling cardamom. Kapha: reserve for occasional use and keep the pieces small.

items.name: Rajgira Ladoo
steps: Toast the popped amaranth over low heat until aromatic, then cool slightly.
Grind or crush it to the texture specified by the style, leaving a little body rather than making a paste.
Warm the ghee with cardamom and combine it with the jaggery.
Mix with the toasted base until the mixture holds when pressed; let it cool enough to handle.
Shape into 12 small balls and allow them to set before serving.
items.guidance: Rajgira Ladoo is a compact traditional sweet; one small piece is the intended serving. Vata: take it warm or at room temperature. Pitta: use the lower sweetener amount and cooling cardamom. Kapha: reserve for occasional use and keep the pieces small.

items.name: Murmura Chikki
steps: Toast the plain puffed rice separately until aromatic, then set aside.
Grease a flat tray lightly with part of the ghee.
Melt the jaggery with the water over low heat and cook until a drop firms when placed in cool water.
Remove from the heat, quickly fold in the toasted ingredients and remaining ghee, and spread the mixture on the tray.
Mark into 12 small pieces while warm, then cool completely before separating the bars.
items.guidance: Murmura Chikki is a crisp jaggery-bound sweet; one small piece is sufficient. Vata: choose a freshly made piece and avoid a very hard texture. Pitta: use the smallest piece and do not add warming spice. Kapha: reserve for occasional use despite the light crisp texture.

items.reviewNote: Modern coconut ladoo often uses condensed milk; this classical-leaning version uses jaggery and ghee, both with verified dravya links.

items.name: Stewed Fruit Bowl
steps: Warm the ghee in a small heavy pan and add the apple and pear.
Turn the fruit gently for two minutes, then add the water and cinnamon.
Cover and cook on low heat until the fruit is tender but still holds some shape.
Stir in the rock sugar and cook uncovered for two minutes until the juices lightly glaze the fruit.
Serve warm on its own, without dairy.
items.guidance: Apples and pears are gently stewed and served without dairy in this warm fruit sweet. Vata: cook until very soft and retain the ghee. Pitta: use little rock sugar. Kapha: omit the rock sugar and take a small bowl.

items.name: Cinnamon Sweet Potato
steps: Steam the sweet-potato wedges for eight minutes so the centers begin to soften.
Arrange them on a warm baking tray and brush with ghee.
Mix the cinnamon, cardamom, and rock sugar and dust the mixture lightly over the wedges.
Bake until the edges color and the centers are completely tender.
Serve warm in small portions.
items.guidance: Pre-steaming keeps these cinnamon sweet-potato wedges soft while a brief bake colors the edges. Vata: retain the ghee and serve warm. Pitta: use half the cinnamon. Kapha: omit the rock sugar and keep the serving small.

items.name: Kesar Shrikhand (Light)
steps: Drain the yogurt in a clean cloth until thick but still creamy.
Warm one spoonful of the drained whey and steep the saffron in it for five minutes.
Whisk the thick yogurt until smooth, then fold in the rock sugar and saffron liquid.
Add the cardamom and pistachios and mix gently.
Serve a small portion at cool room temperature rather than ice-cold.
items.guidance: This shrikhand uses restrained rock sugar and is served in small portions. Vata: serve closer to room temperature. Pitta: retain the saffron and modest sweetness. Kapha: take only a spoonful because the yogurt remains dense.

items.name: Panchamrita
steps: Bring all ingredients to a similar cool room temperature.
Whisk the yogurt smooth in a clean bowl.
Add the milk and ghee and stir until evenly dispersed.
Fold in the rock sugar and raw honey without heating the mixture.
Offer or serve immediately in one small spoonful per person.
items.guidance: Panchamrita is a ritual preparation served by the spoonful, not as a beverage. Vata: take it at room temperature and in the stated tiny portion. Pitta: keep the serving minimal. Kapha: reserve it for ritual use and do not enlarge the portion.
items.reviewNote: Ritual proportions vary. This version keeps honey and ghee unequal by weight and is intended only as a small ceremonial food portion.

items.name: Ukadiche Modak
steps: Cook the coconut and jaggery over low heat until the filling is moist but no longer runny; finish with cardamom.
Bring the water and half the ghee to a boil, stir in the rice flour, cover, and rest off the heat for five minutes.
Knead the warm rice dough until smooth and divide it into twelve portions.
Shape each portion into a cup, add a small spoonful of filling, pleat the rim, and seal the top.
Steam the modak until the shells turn slightly glossy; brush with the remaining ghee and serve warm.
items.guidance: Ukadiche modak are steamed rice-flour dumplings with coconut-jaggery filling. Vata: serve warm with the light ghee brushing. Pitta: keep the jaggery filling modest. Kapha: take one small modak.

items.name: Masala Doodh
steps: Place the milk in a small heavy pan and bring it slowly to a gentle simmer.
Add the almonds, soaked and ground, saffron strands, nutmeg and cook on low heat for five minutes.
Stir in the rock sugar and continue only until the flavor is integrated.
Crush in the cardamom, strain if a smooth drink is desired, and pour into warmed cups.
Serve warm and freshly prepared.
items.guidance: Masala Doodh is a rich warm milk preparation for an occasional small serving. Vata: serve warm and retain the full milk richness. Pitta: favor saffron or cardamom and use little sweetener. Kapha: take a half portion and avoid serving it cold.

items.name: Whole Wheat Panjiri
steps: Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and add the whole-wheat flour.
Roast over low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture becomes aromatic and evenly golden.
Add the almonds, chopped, dry ginger and cook for two more minutes.
Remove from the heat, cool until merely warm, and mix in the jaggery and cardamom.
Break up any clumps and serve one small spoonful at a time.
items.guidance: Whole Wheat Panjiri is a dry roasted flour-and-ghee sweet traditionally served in small spoonfuls. Vata: take with warm milk if suitable. Pitta: moderate ghee and warming spice. Kapha: use a very small portion and reduce sweetener.

items.name: Sesame Almond Panjiri
steps: Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and add the sesame seeds, ground.
Roast over low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture becomes aromatic and evenly golden.
Add the almond meal, dry ginger and cook for two more minutes.
Remove from the heat, cool until merely warm, and mix in the jaggery and cardamom.
Break up any clumps and serve one small spoonful at a time.

Roast over low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture becomes aromatic and evenly golden.
Add the pistachios, chopped, fennel seeds and cook for two more minutes.
Remove from the heat, cool until merely warm, and mix in the jaggery and cardamom.

items.name: Apple Spice Avaleha-Style Preserve
steps: Wash and chop the apples, peeled and chopped, removing any hard seeds or stems.
Simmer it with the water until completely soft, then press or blend to a smooth pulp.
Return the pulp to a heavy pan, add the jaggery, and cook slowly while stirring.
When the mixture becomes glossy and jamlike, stir in the ghee and raisins, dry ginger.
Finish with cardamom and cinnamon, cool completely, and portion with a clean dry spoon.
